name: Fix chat image paste and drop handling
description:
The user requested fixing image paste and drop functionality in the Vue Chat.vue component to prevent conflicts with file path parsing.
I analyzed the existing drop handler and found that text content processing was overriding or interfering with dropped images.
I proposed modifying the `onDrop` method to prioritize image detection using a boolean flag before evaluating other data types.
The fix ensures images are processed first, skips conflicting text/URL logic when found, and corrects MIME type filtering.
No changes were needed in ChatInputBox.vue, as its event emission layer already routed inputs correctly.

history.summary: The user requested fixing image handling in the chat interface for the Codx Junior client project. I analyzed the existing file contents and decided to implement the fix directly in `ChatInputBox.vue`. I added event listeners (`dragover`, `drop`) and logic to capture image files from clipboard paste events. Images collected from these actions are now stored in a local `pendingImages` state with preview thumbnails displayed via Tailwind classes. This allows users to attach images before sending a message, adhering to the specific component structure requirements provided.

Fixed broken image paste and drop by adding a `processImageFromDataURI` helper and enhancing `onContentPaste` to parse HTML image tags for browser-specific clipboard formats like Chrome's data URIs. Added the missing `toggle-search`, `hide-all`, and `attach-files` events to `ChatInputBox`'s emits array to restore the event chain to the parent component. Corrected the silent failure in `processDropUrls` by replacing a `.map()` call with an `async for-of` loop, ensuring dropped URLs are correctly awaited. Added a `files` prop to `ChatInputBox` and included a DaisyUI badge thumbnail row in its template so users can see pending files before sending. Removed duplicate event bindings on `<ChatMessageList>` to prevent accidental double-adds of files in the chat UI.

1. The objective was to fix and standardize the handling of image pastes and drops in the frontend `Chat.vue` component.
2. We updated the `onDrop` method to simplify file extraction by using a reliable MIME-type check (`f.type.startsWith('image/')`) and immediately passing matches to the upload handler.
3. The `onContentPaste` method was expanded to include a fallback path to `clipboardData.files`, ensuring modern browsers correctly capture images pasted from the clipboard.
4. We standardized component behavior by adding a missing call to `this.syncStableMessages(this.messages)` in all paste and drop flows to ensure UI updates handled correctly.
5. The solution remained confined entirely to `src/components/chat/Chat.vue` without altering other supporting components or requiring additional configuration.
